notes: The author calls it an adventure game and models it on a mascot-horror kindergarten, so Adventure leads and Survival is named second for the horror framing; the mode is exactly Survival's Mascot Horror preset, which a secondary genre is allowed to supply. The map is the kindergarten and nothing else — the answers cap it at a handful of connected rooms and the player never goes outside — so interior-single, which costs nothing and needs no outside-to-inside transition. Two changes to the preset, both from the prompt: cover-los is dropped because the monster explicitly cannot kill you, so there is nothing to break line of sight from, and the monster itself is npc-population rather than spawner-npc for the same reason — it inhabits and watches rather than entering a fight. With no user to ask I read the remote-operated buttons as door mechanisms (gate-progression) and kept gate-escape as the place the run ends, since the layout needs a terminating exit even though the prompt never says how the game is won.
